title: Compatible pointed polynomial strict-local closed-fibre comparisons
statement: Let S and V be schemes, r a natural number, E=ULift(Fin r), e:V isomorphic to affine E-space over S, and v:Spec Omega to V with Omega algebraically closed. Use the explicit A, B, a, t, I, J, P and L and the conclusion-data type FibreModels of [def-trf-affine-coordinate-strict-local-data], with its canonical geometric evaluations. Suppose A has its local-ring structure and epsilon_B(t_i)=0 for each i in K. Then FibreModels with these actual rings, ideals, canonical coefficient map A to kappa to P, polynomial variables, structural coordinates and geometric evaluations is inhabited. In particular it supplies both pointed algebraic strict-henselization presentations and the unique residue-compatible comparison of the two closed-fibre quotients. It makes no assertion about the coordinate-zero immersion in V, its universal test-scheme property, the factorization of v, or the quotient strict local ring B/J.

proof.text: Factor the canonical evaluation A to Omega through kappa=A/m_A; its kernel is m_A. Evaluate P=kappa[T_i] at the images of the coordinates t_i. The hypothesis epsilon_B(t_i)=0 for i in K implies L is contained in the prime evaluation kernel q. The quotient evaluation on P/L has prime kernel equal to the image q/L by the ideal correspondence for a surjective quotient.

Base change e to Spec A and then Spec kappa. By the affine-space pullback universal property and AffineSpace.SpecIso, the resulting closed fibre is Spec P with its specified coordinate sections. Apply the smooth closed-fibre comparison to the affine-space projection. Compose its isomorphism B/(m_A B) with the affine strict-local comparison on Spec P at the polynomial evaluation point to obtain H0 and iso0. Use the defining pointed-etale colimit as its presentation. Both comparisons preserve coefficients, variables and geometric evaluations, giving their recorded equations.

Apply the closed-immersion strict-localization Cartesian comparison to Spec(P/L) in Spec P. Its ideal in H0 is generated by the images of selected t_i. The inverse image of this ideal in B is m_A B+J: lift the coefficients in a finite sum of multiples along the surjection B to B/(m_A B). This identifies the successive quotient with B/(m_A B+J). Apply the affine strict-local comparison on Spec(P/L) to construct H1, its pointed presentation, iso1 and its coefficient, surviving-coordinate and evaluation equations.

The prime-localization residue-field embeddings are induced by the two geometric polynomial evaluations into Omega. Restrict to their relative separable closures in Omega; the scalar towers use the localization residue maps. This gives the specified residue equations. Conjugate the functorial strict-local map by the two affine comparisons to obtain the local comparison H0 to H1. Both maps from B are functorial restriction maps, hence the quotient square and evaluation square commute. Any other local map satisfying the polynomial equation agrees on P_q by localization uniqueness; the residue equation fixes its map of separable closures inside Omega. Strict-henselization functorial uniqueness then proves comparison_unique.
